title: Planetary floral kingdom roster
scope: Roster of major producer and decomposer kingdoms for Project Hearthway's planet at growth-strategy-theme level; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: The planet's macroscopic producer and decomposer life is organised across six major kingdoms at growth-strategy-theme level, with familiar ecological roles distributed originally rather than copied from Earth clades.
K1, networked modular flora, comprises forms whose living subsurface networks link rooted growth modules; the reserve-web guild governed by the existing reserve-web records belongs to this kingdom.
K2, tower flora, comprises long-lived, tall, self-supporting woody-analogue structural forms.
K3, free-seeder flora, comprises short-lived, unnetworked, fast-dispersing individual plants.
K4, water flora, comprises submerged, floating, and wet-margin producers.
K5, crust-and-cushion flora, comprises low, slow, surface-hugging pioneer growth.
K6, thread decomposers, comprises non-photosynthesising thread-and-body networks occupying decomposer, recycler, and mutualist roles.
Every kingdom includes abundant ordinary, unremarkable forms; no kingdom exists only to supply spectacular flora.
boundaries: Kingdom codes and functional labels are author-facing shorthand, not in-world names, formal taxonomy, or cladistic claims; final names remain protected unknowns.

The roster fixes qualitative growth-strategy themes only; energy capture, chemistry, anatomy, reproduction, dispersal, seasonality, defences, and Mana patterns remain open except where existing bounded records govern.
Woody-analogue establishes no Earth wood, bark, or tree homology; thread decomposers establishes no Earth fungus homology; plants and flora are functional conveniences, not Earth-clade claims.
No kingdom is established as present, dominant, or absent at any particular location, including the initial basin, beyond what existing records already establish.

The western temperate rainforest, basin woodland, wet-margin and marsh vegetation, and the sturdy egg-substrate plants referenced by canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/basin-lake-spring-breeding-pulse are not assigned to kingdoms by this record.
Microscopic producer and decomposer life and rare minor or relict kingdoms below the roster's grain remain possible but require their own records.
Cross-kingdom symbioses, including any root partnership between K6 and producer kingdoms, remain open possibilities, not established relationships.
No domesticate, crop, harvest practice, or other human-use relationship is established.
Earth life of any era and mythological flora may inspire author-facing design; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted directly.
No Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, spawn point, refill node, guaranteed harvest, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Water, light or other energy, nutrients, space, growth time, disturbance, disease, and decay remain binding ecological constraints for every kingdom.
story_implications: Scene vegetation can be designed kingdom-first from stable growth-strategy slots with Earth inspiration kept author-facing.
Forage, harvest, timber-analogue, and material-culture development gains stable botanical structure without premature species claims.
Decomposition, soil renewal, and symbiosis stories gain a dedicated kingdom slot.
Every particular guild, species, local presence, and human use requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The roster describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, guaranteed harvest, spawn source, refill node, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What deep divergence history produced the six kingdoms, and how do they relate to the faunal lineages' history?
Which kingdoms hold the rainforest, woodland, wet-margin, and egg-substrate vegetation?
What energy capture, chemistry, reproduction, and dispersal patterns characterise each kingdom?
Which cross-kingdom symbioses exist, and at what cost?
Which kingdoms supply crops, forage, timber-analogues, fibres, and medicines for later cultural development?
Which minor or relict kingdoms, if any, persist below the roster's grain?

author_approval.evidence: After the A/B/C floral-roster options were presented with A recommended, the Author selected 'A — Six kingdoms' on 2026-08-17.
